title: Knowledge authoring result
description: Result contract for the knowledge-author agent, the named producer. The named consumer is the ingestion procedure, which reads the closed `state` field to tell an authored object from a blocked one and moves to the next entry either way. This artifact carries control flow, so it requires this versioned schema and boundary validation before consumption.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

producer.description: The agent this contract belongs to. A const, not a free string: a result claiming another producer is not an instance of this contract.

state.description: The closed set the consumer branches on: authored = a new knowledge object exists, updated = an existing one was revised, blocked = nothing was written and blocking_reason says why.

request.description: What was delegated, so a result can be traced to its request without reading either.

node_type.description: Which of the six types the vocabulary to. Recorded because the per-type conditionals differ enough that a consumer resolving the object needs to know which branch governs it before reading the file.

object_id.description: Id of the knowledge object written, matching the id shape of schemas/knowledge-object.json.

object_path.description: Repository-relative path of the knowledge file written.

files_changed.description: Every file the agent touched. This is the evidence trail a reviewer diffs against. A derived projection is never in this list: those the materializer's output, and an agent that wrote one would be hand-editing a derived artifact.

blocking_reason.description: Why nothing was written: the missing input, the contradicting object, or the domain fact the request did not supply — named so the caller can act without re-running the agent to find out.
A blocking reason on a successful result is a contradiction; expressed as a dependency so the failure names the offending field.
